Best Roasting Pan for Thanksgiving: Circulon vs Cuisinart vs the Enamel Workhorse (2026)

The pan decides two things: how the bird cooks and how you spend the evening after. These three sit at the center of our roasting-pan picks — a nonstick weeknight-er, an uncoated gravy machine, and a big enamel workhorse with a lid.

Published November 17, 2026 · Ratings and review counts pulled from Amazon listings via the official affiliate API on November 17, 2026 · We don't handle or test products — we curate highly rated, well-reviewed ones and compare what the data says

A roasting pan is the one piece of Thanksgiving equipment nobody wants to discover is wrong at 2pm. The decision tree is shorter than the marketing makes it look: coated or uncoated, rack or no rack, and will it fit your oven with a 15-pound bird on it.

Circulon Total Bakeware 17×13 Nonstick Roaster (with Rack)

4.7★ from 9,114 ratings — the most-reviewed nonstick roaster on our curated list. Ridged walls are designed to reduce sticking and scorching, the rack lifts the bird out of drippings, and the whole thing goes in the dishwasher, which on November 26th is not a small feature.

Best for: the cleanup-realistic host. One less thing to scrub the night before guests arrive.

Cuisinart Chef's Classic 16″ Roasting Pan (with Rack)

4.7★ from 5,807 ratings — uncoated stainless over an encapsulated-aluminum base. That matters for one specific thing people argue about every Thanksgiving: fond. Bare metal builds the brown sticky layer that turns into pan gravy; nonstick mostly doesn't.

Best for: the gravy traditionalist who wants drippings worth deglazing.

18″ Enamel Roaster with Lid

4.5★ from 218 ratings — smaller sample, so weigh it accordingly: an 18-inch oval rated for birds in the ~22 lb class, plus a lid that does double duty (brining in the fridge, leftovers as storage). Enamel sits between the other two: easier to clean than bare steel, more forgiving than premium nonstick.

Best for: big-turkey households and anyone who hates buying a separate storage container.

Quick Verdict

🏆 Our Pick for Most Homes: Circulon Total Nonstick 17×13

It wins on volume, consistency, and the unglamorous stuff: 9,114 ratings at 4.7 stars, a rack that actually lifts, and a dishwasher-friendly finish. Choose Cuisinart if pan gravy is a family religion (bare stainless builds fond; nonstick fights you). Choose the enamel 18-incher if the bird is enormous or the lid saves you a container.

The Real Question: Coated or Bare

Nonstick earns its keep on the one night you're washing the most dishes of the year. Bare stainless earns its keep at 11am, when the drippings under a nonstick pan stay pale and under a steel pan turn mahogany — that brown layer is flavor, and gravy people can tell. There is no wrong answer, only a wrong expectation.

Size Is an Oven Problem, Not a Turkey Problem

An 18-inch oval fits a 20-plus-pound bird but fights a narrow oven rack; a 16×13 sits flat in almost everything. Measure the widest thing your oven holds before you measure the turkey. The enamel pick's lid is quietly the best value feature of the three — brining overnight in the pan, storing leftovers in the same pan, no separate purchase.

What the Numbers Say

The two 4.7s (9,114 and 5,807 ratings) are established listings — that's a lot of households agreeing. The enamel's 4.5 across 218 is real but thinner evidence, which we'd normally discount; it stays in the comparison because the lid-plus-capacity combo has no substitute at its price point.

Which One Should You Buy?

Circulon — first Thanksgiving you're hosting, dishwasher realist, wants the safe volume pick.

Cuisinart — gravy from scratch, non-negotiable. This is the fond pan.

Enamel 18″ — huge bird, tight budget, or you're tired of storing leftovers in foil.
